prompt:
<user_input mode="act">Make the following changes to HintLab in this repo (/Users/prakharagarwal/ClineHackathon), in priority order. Do not modify anything under cline-proof/ (except that README text may describe it). Never modify, write, copy, move or delete anything in ~/.cline, and never print any token or secret.

1. Clear message when the tutor model is not authenticated. When the Cline SDK cannot authenticate (no credentials, expired or invalid login, missing or wrong API key for the chosen provider), HintLab must say so clearly instead of failing generically:
   - Find the real error shape by reading the installed @cline/sdk and its dependency packages in node_modules (the error classes, messages, status codes or fields thrown or emitted when credentials are missing or rejected, both at session start and as subscribe error events). Do not inspect ~/.cline to do this.
   - Add a small detector that recognises those auth failures (missing credentials, HTTP 401/403, invalid or expired token or key) and maps them to one short message, exactly: Tutor not connected: run cline auth (see README). Put the exact text in one exported constant so the server, SSE and UI all use the same wording (you may wrap "cline auth" in backticks in the constant if it renders well in the README and UI, but keep it identical everywhere).
   - The server log must print that line once per failed session (with the session id), without stack traces or secrets.
   - The SSE error event for that session must carry that short message (and a machine-readable code such as auth so the UI can recognise it), and the session status must end as an error rather than hanging.
   - The web page must show that friendly message in its error area (instead of the generic "Something went wrong"), keep the test results visible, and leave the Run button usable so the student can retry after authenticating.
   - Other errors keep their current friendly messages.
   - Verify the error path without touching ~/.cline: add a check script and npm script named check:auth that starts the server on PORT=3200 in a child process whose environment forces an unauthenticated provider, for example by setting HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID to a provider that needs an API key (such as anthropic) with HINTLAB_MODEL_ID set to one of its models and no key available, or by pointing the SDK at an empty temporary config/data directory if the SDK supports such an override through config or an environment variable (only if that does not read or change ~/.cline). If you add a new override for the provider API key or the config/data directory, document it. The check must POST /api/session, read the SSE stream, and assert that an error event with the auth code and the exact message arrives within a reasonable timeout, that the server log contains the line, and that no hint was produced. It must stop the server by PID. Report exactly how the check forces the failure and what raw SDK error it saw (with any secret redacted).

2. README: add an API-key path for judges who do not have ClinePass. Run cline auth --help yourself and use only the flags it actually lists. Give one concrete example that authenticates the Cline CLI with a provider plus an API key (for example Anthropic or an OpenAI-compatible provider such as OpenRouter, using a placeholder key and a real model id for that provider), then explain how to point HintLab at it with HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID and HINTLAB_MODEL_ID (with matching example values), and how to confirm it works (start the server and run check:agent). Say which provider ids and model ids the code accepts and where the credentials are then stored, without showing secrets. If HintLab also supports passing a key directly through an environment variable, document it; if not, say so.

3. README ports: change the suggested override port and the address-already-in-use (EADDRINUSE) fix from 3200 to 3300, and add a note that the check scripts (check:agent, check:web, check:auth) use port 3200, so do not run the server on 3200 while running them.

4. README accuracy: the minimal-environment sentence currently claims student code cannot see the server environment or ~/.cline. Remove the ~/.cline claim. State honestly that student code runs with a minimal environment (only PATH, HOME set to the run's temp dir, and LANG), in a fresh temp directory per run, with timeouts, process-group cleanup and an output cap, but that it is not OS-sandboxed yet: it still runs as the host user and could read files that user can read. Check the rest of the README for any other overclaim about isolation and fix it the same way.

5. README polish:
   - Add a curl example that creates a session with POST /api/session for sum-of-list (using the starter code) and then follows the SSE stream for the returned session id, plus a curl example of next-hint. Make sure the example works as written against the server on port 3300.
   - In the macOS Node install steps, note that brew link for node@22 may need the force flag.
   - Use a placeholder for the clone URL, and make the cloned folder name consistent everywhere in the README.
   - Update the project layout tree and the "How this was built" list so they include steps 04 and 05 and every prompt file actually present in cline-proof/prompts/ (list the directory to get them right, including 00b, 02c, 03-web-ui.retry and 03r), and the cline-proof/screens/ folder. Do not list cline-proof/reference/sdk-check, which was removed.

Port rule: another test run is using port 3100 and the directory /tmp/hl-test. Never touch, kill, signal or bind to anything on port 3100 or in /tmp/hl-test, and use no broad pkill patterns. Use PORT=3200 for check scripts and 3300 only for checking the README curl example; stop only processes you started, by PID. Leave no server running.

Verify before finishing: npm run typecheck, npm run test:runner, npm run check:auth, and npm run check:agent (real model call, to prove normal auth still works). Fix anything that fails. Report the files changed, the new README auth section verbatim, the exact new error text, and how check:auth forced and observed the auth failure.</user_input>

metadata.systemPrompt:
You are Cline, an AI coding agent. Your primary goal is to assist users with various coding tasks by leveraging your knowledge and the tools at your disposal. Given the user's prompt, you should use the tools available to you to answer user's question.

Always gather all the necessary context before starting to work on a task. For example, if you are generating a unit test or new code, make sure you understand the requirement, the naming conventions, frameworks and libraries used and aligned in the current codebase, and the environment and commands used to run and test the code etc. Always validate the new unit test at the end including running the code if possible for live feedback.
Review each question carefully and answer it with detailed, accurate information.
If you need more information, use one of the available tools or ask for clarification instead of making assumptions or lies.

Environment you are running in:
<env>
1. Platform: darwin
2. Date: 10/4/2026
3. IDE: Terminal Shell
4. Working Directory: /Users/prakharagarwal/ClineHackathon
</env>

Remember:
- Always adhere to existing code conventions and patterns.
- Use only libraries and frameworks that are confirmed to be in use in the current codebase.
- Provide complete and functional code without omissions or placeholders.
- Be explicit about any assumptions or limitations in your solution.
- Always show your planning process before executing any task. This will help ensure that you have a clear understanding of the requirements and that your approach aligns with the user's needs.
- Always use absolute paths when referring to files.
- You can call multiple tools in a single response. Before using tools, identify every independent read, search, command, or edit needed for the next step and emit all of those tool calls now, either as multiple tool calls or as one batched input for tools that accept arrays. Do not wait for one independent result before requesting another. Do not split independent reads, searches, checks, or edits across separate turns.
- Good parallelism examples: read all known relevant files in one read_files call; run independent inspection commands in one run_commands call; emit independent read_files, search_codebase, and run_commands calls together in one response; emit multiple editor calls together when editing different files or non-overlapping regions.
- Always verify the files you have edited or created at the end of the task to ensure they are completed and working as expected.

Begin by analyzing the user's input and gathering any necessary additional context. Then, present your plan at the start of your response along with tool calls before proceeding with the task. It's OK for this section to be quite long.

REMEMBER, be helpful and proactive! Don't ask for permission to do something when you can do it! Do not indicates you will be using a tool unless you are actually going to use it.

IMPORTANT: Always includes tool calls in your response until the task is completed. Response without tool calls will considered as completed with final answer.

When you have completed the task, please provide a summary of what you did and any relevant information that the user should know. This will help ensure that the user understands the changes made and can easily follow up if they have any questions or need further assistance. Do not indicate that you will perform an action without actually doing it. Always provide the final result in your response. Always validate your answer with checking the code and running it if possible. 

If user asked a simple question without any coding context, answer it directly without using any tools.
# Plan / Act Modes

User messages arrive wrapped in a <user_input mode="..."> tag. The mode attribute is the interaction mode the user was in when they sent that message: "plan" means plan-mode constraints applied (explore, analyze, and align on a plan -- no edits or state-changing commands), while "act" (or "yolo") means implementation was allowed. If the mode attribute changes between messages, the user switched modes -- the newest message's mode is what governs right now, regardless of what earlier messages allowed. A <mode_notice> block inside a message marks exactly when such a switch happened.

# Workspace Configuration
{
  "workspaces": {
    "/Users/prakharagarwal/ClineHackathon": {
      "hint": "ClineHackathon",
      "latestGitCommitHash": "960e2d89e617c7ef8fa149ab8af94da0bff36304",
      "latestGitBranchName": "main"
    }
  }
}
